title: A Horizon for the Compass
premise: Mirabel Sterling, a railroad engineer haunted by the collapse he survived and the men who didn't, drifts along closed rail lines keeping his name out of ledgers and his past off paper. When a dying prospector named Eben Crow trades him a hand-drawn map to an uncharted river source for a promise—that Mirabel will deliver it to Crow's estranged daughter—Mirabel inherits both a debt and a target, because others killed for that map before. Pursued by the survey crew whose greed caused his disaster years ago, Mirabel follows the river upstream through canyon and winter, forced at last to claim his real name. At the source he finds not gold but water rights worth fortunes, delivers the map to Crow's daughter, and chooses to stand trial for his old failure rather than vanish again—buying with exposure the peace invisibility never gave him.
about_author: Isandro Joubert is the pen name of a former surveyor's assistant who spent six seasons mapping river basins in the high country before turning to fiction. He writes adventure novels about people whose professions demand precision but whose lives refuse it.

chapters.title: The Man Who Rode the Dead Lines
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. He rides a decommissioned handcar down a closed mountain line, repairing trestles for cash under false names, establishing his ritual of constant motion and his terror of being recorded anywhere. Emotional beat: weary competence masking dread; a newspaper clipping about a bridge collapse shows what he's running from.

chapters.title: A Trade at Dusk
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. At a way station he finds prospector Eben Crow gut-shot and dying; Crow trades his map of the river's forbidden source for a promise of delivery to his daughter in Calder Junction. Emotional beat: reluctant compassion; Mirabel accepts the promise knowing promises leave paper trails, and buries Crow as riders pass on the ridge.

chapters.title: What the Map Wouldn't Say
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, studying the map by firelight: precise engineering notation he recognizes—the draftsman is someone from his old crew. Flashback threads reveal the collapsed trestle and the survey crew's falsified load reports. Emotional beat: dawning connection between his past and this map; he realizes staying invisible was already over.

chapters.title: Riders on the Water Grade
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Men from the Halloway Survey Company board a train he's riding, checking passengers against a description. He slips off at a water stop and begins upriver on foot. Emotional beat: hunted adrenaline sharpening into resolve; first direct contact with antagonist Silas Halloway's lieutenant, Voss.

chapters.title: Calder Junction
chapters.summary: Delia Crow's POV. Crow's daughter, a telegraph operator who believes her father abandoned her, receives a wire meant for Mirabel and decodes its warning. She decides to intercept the stranger carrying her father's map. Emotional beat: anger braided with grief; she wants answers more than inheritance.

chapters.title: The Crossing at Gray Fork
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Delia catches up to Mirabel at a flooded crossing; they save each other from the rapids and trade truths—she learns her father died keeping the map from Halloway, and Mirabel admits his name and his crime. Emotional beat: guarded alliance forming; two liars recognizing each other's weight.

chapters.title: Winter in the Narrows
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Snow traps them in a canyon; Voss's crew closes in behind and a rockslide ahead blocks retreat. Starved and freezing, Mirabel confesses fully the twenty-one men lost to his signed inspection. Emotional beat: despair transmuting into purpose—he stops running toward escape and starts moving toward reckoning.

chapters.title: The Source
chapters.summary: Mirabel and Delia's POV. They reach the headwaters: a spring feeding the whole valley, which Halloway intends to dam and sell, strangling every town downstream. They find evidence Crow gathered to expose him—and realize the map was always testimony, not treasure. Emotional beat: awe curdling into fury; the price of survival reframed as the cost of silence.

chapters.title: Halloway's Dam
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POV. Voss corners them at the spring; Halloway arrives to buy their silence. Mirabel uses his engineer's knowledge to breach Halloway's survey equipment and flood the camp records, while Delia wires the truth downstream from Crow's hidden line. Emotional beat: Mirabel choosing visibility—giving his real name aloud to Halloway before witnesses.

chapters.title: A Horizon for the Compass
chapters.summary: Resolution, Mirabel's POV. Halloway is arrested on federal water-rights charges; Mirabel surrenders to face inquiry over the old collapse, exonerated when Delia's father's papers prove the falsified reports. He rides the dead lines one last time—not fleeing, but mapping which ones to rebuild. Emotional beat: quiet earned peace; motion chosen, not imposed.
